answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake bond before it may trade. Forging identities then stops being free: every fake copy must post its own bond, like laying a separate marble foundation under each shopfront instead of pitching tents on a dune. If an agent cheats, its bond is slashed and burned, leaving only an ember of the deposit, while honest agents reclaim theirs in full. An attacker must therefore risk real capital per identity, so creating ten thousand Sybils costs ten thousand bonds, while one honest agent pays only once.
